positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: "2023 was a big year for Alaska. I’ve worked together with our Senators to bring home historic amounts of funding, jobs, and infrastructure projects – I’m excited to see what we can do in 2024!"
"Mary has been working with the rest of the congressional delegation and the state government to implement a bipartisan infrastructure bill and bring over $2 billion in investments to our state."

"Two years ago, today, the Bipartisan Infrastructure bill became law. Don Young helped get it passed in the House. Now, I’m working with our Senators to get that funding into Alaskan pockets. Only a tag-team effort could make this generational impact on Alaska’s infrastructure."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "Alaska’s villages are facing a crisis in housing. I spoke on the House floor yesterday advocating for reauthorizing the Native American Housing and Self Determination Act"
"Fighting for affordable, accessible housing statewide."

"Visiting MyHouse Mat-Su was an inspiring experience--this center is an excellent example of how to support homeless youth, and the importance of wrap-around services. We must address Alaska's long-term housing shortage, but also support those who have nowhere to go right now."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "As a born and raised rural Alaskan, I understand how hard inflation hits our communities. Costs of things like fruit & coffee were already too high. That’s why I'm going to Congress. I’m going to do everything I can to lower prices and bring our costs back down."
"Fighting inflation and doing everything we can to make the goods we buy affordable and accessible."
"I firmly believe that any and all efforts to reduce inflation and drive down our national deficit are good efforts, given that doing so betters the lives of regular Alaskans."

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

evidence.text: "Yes! I absolutely support student loan reform. College should be affordable for people seeking higher education. Allowing people to be crushed by the weight of insurmountable debt is not how we set our future generations up for success."
Rated 100% by National Education Association

positions.question: Do you support government funding for the development of renewable energy (e.g. solar, wind, geo-thermal)?

evidence.text: "Alaskans are resilient – why should our energy grid be any different? Robust transmission and storage will make more renewable energy possible and bring cheaper, more reliable electricity to Alaskans. The $206M grant announced in October will make that future possible."

"Friendly reminder that the Federal government is investing more in Alaskan renewable energy capabilities than ever before, but we need the state to match those funds to secure all the affordable and renewable energy we can get. Governing is all about partnerships!"
Rated 87% by League of Conservation Voters

positions.question: Do you support the federal government allowing permits for drilling on public lands?

evidence.text: "Alaska’s standards for environmental impact are world-leading. It’s essential to complete the process of getting good projects greenlighted. Willow passed that process multiple times, and I’m ready to see boots on the ground and oil in our pipeline."

"It looks like jobs, revenue, and economic investment are under the tree for Alaska this year! I'm grateful for the hard work we Alaskans put in all year to get Willow across the finish line--we're seeing the benefits already."

"One year ago, I stood on this stage at Alaska Oil and Gas Association as a candidate and promised to work to get Willow approved. I kept that promise, and we’re just getting started. Alaska must be a leader in energy production again, and I’m excited for what we will do next."
Voted against HR 1: "Lower Energy Costs Act"

positions.question: Do you generally support gun-control legislation (e.g. red flag laws, boyfriend loopholes)?

evidence.text: Anchorage Daily News: "Guns are a part of Alaska’s culture and a core tool of a subsistence lifestyle. I grew up hunting, my husband is a big game hunting advocate and I will continue to own guns and support the right of Alaskans to own guns. But it’s past time our nation’s leaders put forth more than just words to address the grief we all share. We can take common sense action, and we must. Provisions like secure storage laws, reasonable waiting periods and universal background checks can make all of us safer while still preserving the rights guaranteed by the Second Amendment."
Rated 17% by National Rifle Association

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: "Healthcare shouldn’t be something anyone has to declare bankruptcy over."
"Making sure healthcare is accessible regardless of how much money is in our bank accounts will not only make the lives of millions in our country better but also likely save lives in the process."
"We shouldn’t have to max out our credit cards or wipe out our savings for healthcare — including dental, vision, and hearing."
"Social Security and Medicare should never be on the chopping block when we talk about "balancing the budget"

positions.question: Do you support expanding paid family AND/OR medical leave benefits (e.g. maternity leave)?

evidence.text: "A reminder that rail workers across the country have been working the past few months with 0 days of paid sick leave for their work. The backbone of our economy, working without even a single guaranteed paid sick day. Think about that."

"Making sure rail workers have paid sick leave and can be a healthier, safer workforce is critical to our economic security. I don’t want an entire sector of workers to have to show up to work sick, especially workers so critical to our supply chain. They need paid sick leave."
"Making sure workers, especially workers in critical sectors, are healthy with paid sick leave and not showing up to work sick to avoid penalties is one part of that"

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "Bringing down the price of the prescription drugs Alaskans rely on to stay healthy."
Voted in favor of HR 5378: "Lower Costs, More Transparency Act"

positions.question: Do you support increasing security along the southern US border?

"Thank you #FoxNewsLive & @GriffJenkins for having me on to talk about why additional border security isn’t just needed in the south but in the west as well. Ensuring that the U.S. invests in additional military & infrastructure projects in the Arctic is one of my top priorities!"
